memos.headline: Copart: founder-CEO takes $1 salary and 20M options struck $26-$53
reasoning: Quote: 'approved the grant to A. Jayson Adair, the Company's Chief Executive Officer, of a nonstatutory stock option to purchase 20,000,000 shares'
Quote: tranches at '$26.27 ... $35.03 ... $43.78 ... and $52.54 per share'; 'a salary of $1 each year' and no bonus or other equity for 10 years
Quote: 'subject to approval by the Company's stockholders'; vests on the 5th anniversary
New: filed Friday 16:02 after the close; first public account found is this filing. Not yet traded
Context: Adair returned as CEO July 31, 2026; he took a $1-salary option package once before, in 2009
Tape: 26.27 on Oct 14 (the grant-date strike), 27.75 on Oct 15 (+5.6%, 2.1x volume), 27.89 on Oct 16
objections: SCOUT: Thursday's +5.6% on 2.1x volume came before this filing; cause unknown

memos.headline: Long CPRT: the founder bets ten years of pay on a double
reasoning: All of the CEO's pay for a decade now depends on the stock: three of four tranches are struck 33-100% above the grant price
The 2009 version of this deal preceded years of strong returns; it reads as conviction, not a payday
What the market must believe: this is a routine pay item. It is not routine for a $26B company
Dilution is about 2% of shares and only realized if the stock rises a lot
Direction long, horizon 10 trading days
Wrong if: the proxy advisers oppose it and the vote becomes a fight, or the market reads it as governance risk
objections: SCOUT: Thursday's +5.6% on 2.1x volume came before this filing; cause unknown

memos.headline: Mega-grants usually draw governance fire. Direction is a coin flip.
reasoning: ANALYST reads conviction. Proxy advisers and many holders read a 20M-share grant to a founder as overpay and entrenchment; recent mega-grants have drawn votes against and lawsuits
The first tranche is struck at $26.27, the Oct 14 close, after a slide. Setting the strike the day the stock was low is not conviction, it is a good price
The vote is not done; a contested vote is a headline risk before any upside
Thursday's +5.6% on twice normal volume before the filing is unexplained; ANALYST cannot say the news is fully fresh
Without a reliable sign on direction there is nothing for QUANT to size
Track record: 22 past cases, none with 5 days of history. No evidence that my kills are too strict yet
objections: SCOUT: Thursday's +5.6% on 2.1x volume came before this filing; cause unknown
SKEPTIC 1: market reaction to founder mega-grants is not reliably positive
SKEPTIC 2: first strike set at a local low
SKEPTIC 3: shareholder vote still to come
